intro: Mbissel is a village in the M'bour department of Senegal, on the road that runs between Joal and Fimela near the coast south of Dakar. Beside that road stands a baobab whose trunk is a grey wall of swollen ribs and bulges, with roots snaking over bare sandy ground and people sitting in its shade. A reader sent us its photograph and calls it the largest baobab in Senegal, a claim the page gives as theirs.

trees.story:
A reader sent this baobab with a GPS fix taken beside it, on the road between Joal and Fimela near Mbissel, in the M'bour department of Senegal, with one line: “This is the largest Baobab in Senegal.” They gave it an age of between 580 and 850 years.

The photograph shows why someone would say so. The trunk is not one column but a wall of them, grey and smooth and swollen, folded into great vertical ribs and bulges, with a knotted burr the size of a person near its foot. Roots snake out across the bare, sandy ground. Limbs as thick as ordinary trees leave the trunk at head height and spread into a leafy crown. In its shade a man sits on a chair, and a white plastic chair stands empty against the trunk, which dwarfs both.

The largest in Senegal is the reader's claim, and we have not yet checked it against a survey; the age is their estimate too, so read both as theirs. The tree is an African baobab, Adansonia digitata, as the trunk and its leaves show. If you have measured it, tell us here.

Look for the ribbed grey wall by the road.
